_comment: Router port-forwarding instructions. Adding a router is a pull request, not a release.
Matching is tried in this order, most reliable first:
vendor  - substring of the manufacturer the router reports over UPnP. Most reliable.
banner  - substring of the gateway admin page title or Server header. Used when UPnP is off.
oui     - first three octets of the gateway MAC, lowercase colon-separated. Works when
the router answers nothing at all, but only identifies the vendor.
OUI lists are sparse on purpose: a wrong prefix produces confidently wrong instructions,
which is worse than the generic fallback. Only add prefixes you have verified on hardware.
Menu paths vary by firmware version. Keep 'note' for the step people actually get stuck on.

asus.name: ASUS
asus.note: Set 'Enable Port Forwarding' to Yes before the table will accept rows.
asus.reservationPath: LAN → DHCP Server → Manually Assigned IP around the DHCP list

tplink.name: TP-Link
tplink.note: Some Archer firmware calls this 'Port Forwarding' instead of 'Virtual Servers'.
tplink.reservationPath: Advanced → Network → DHCP Server → Address Reservation

netgear.name: NETGEAR
netgear.path: Advanced → Advanced Setup → Port Forwarding / Port Triggering
netgear.note: Choose 'Port Forwarding' rather than 'Port Triggering' — they are different features.
netgear.reservationPath: Advanced → Setup → LAN Setup → Address Reservation

fritzbox.name: FRITZ!Box
fritzbox.note: Turn on the Advanced View first, or Port Sharing is hidden.
fritzbox.reservationPath: Home Network → Network → the device's Edit pencil → 'Always assign the same IPv4 address'

linksys.name: Linksys
linksys.path: Security → Apps and Gaming → Single Port Forwarding

ubiquiti.name: Ubiquiti UniFi
ubiquiti.note: Older controllers put this under Settings → Routing & Firewall.
ubiquiti.reservationPath: Client Devices → the device → Settings → Fixed IP Address

mikrotik.name: MikroTik
mikrotik.path: IP → Firewall → NAT → add a dst-nat rule
mikrotik.note: Set chain to dstnat, protocol tcp, dst-port to the port below, then action=dst-nat with the address and port below.
mikrotik.reservationPath: IP → DHCP Server → Leases → make the lease static

synology.name: Synology Router
synology.reservationPath: Network Center → DHCP Server → DHCP Clients → Add to reservation

eero.name: eero
eero.path: eero app → Settings → Network Settings → Reservations & Port Forwarding
eero.note: eero requires the mobile app; there is no web admin page.
eero.reservationPath: the same screen — the reservation is created alongside the forward

google.name: Google Nest Wifi
google.path: Google Home app → Wi-Fi → Settings → Advanced networking → Port management
google.note: Google Home requires a reserved address before it will offer the device for port forwarding.

_default.name: your router
_default.path: the section called 'Port Forwarding', 'Virtual Server', 'NAT', or 'Applications & Gaming'
_default.note: Menu names vary between manufacturers and firmware versions.
_default.reservationPath: the DHCP settings, usually called 'Address Reservation' or 'Static Lease'
